vision.paraphrase: Version reporting is named as a cross-cutting concern, so anyone can check which build is deployed.

claude_md.paraphrase: The HTTP server publishes its name and semantic version at a public endpoint so a deployment can be checked without signing in.

vision.paraphrase: Version reporting is a cross-cutting concern, and one version should be visible through every channel.

claude_md.paraphrase: The MCP initialize handshake must carry the same version as the public version endpoint, so clients and operators agree.

vision.paraphrase: Version reporting is a cross-cutting concern that also covers the local stdio binary.

claude_md.paraphrase: The stdio server prints a single name-and-version line for its version flag and exits 0, which is the CLI form of version exposure.

vision.paraphrase: Version reporting is a cross-cutting concern that covers the stdio server as well as the gateway.

claude_md.paraphrase: The stdio handshake reports the same version that the version flag prints.

vision.paraphrase: The vision requires version exposure in the log, so every log file names the build that wrote it.

claude_md.paraphrase: The gateway's first startup record names the product and its semantic version.

vision.paraphrase: Version exposure in logs is a cross-cutting concern that also covers the stdio server.

claude_md.paraphrase: The stdio server's first startup record names the product and its semantic version.

vision.paraphrase: Logging is a cross-cutting concern that the vision sets as plain text, never carrying narration text, tokens or keys.

claude_md.paraphrase: Every gateway log record uses the project's plain-text layout of timestamp, three-letter level and message.

vision.paraphrase: Logging is a cross-cutting concern, and the vision names a daily file alongside stderr for the gateway.

claude_md.paraphrase: Gateway logs go to a daily rolling file under logs/ as well as to stderr, the configured sink pair for the convention.

vision.paraphrase: Logging is a cross-cutting concern that covers the stdio server's own log stream and file.

claude_md.paraphrase: The stdio server writes plain-text records to stderr and to a daily file, following the same logging layout as the gateway.

vision.paraphrase: Errors must name the problem and the next action, which applies to a bad command-line invocation too.

claude_md.paraphrase: An invalid invocation of the stdio server exits with code 2 and names the next step on stderr.

vision.paraphrase: Logging to stderr and a file is a cross-cutting concern, which keeps the stdio protocol channel clean.

claude_md.paraphrase: The stdio server writes only MCP JSON-RPC messages to stdout and sends every log and diagnostic line to stderr.

vision.paraphrase: Logging to stderr and a file is a cross-cutting concern for the gateway as well.

claude_md.paraphrase: The gateway writes nothing to stdout, so all of its diagnostics stay on stderr and in the log file.

vision.paraphrase: The vision requires tool errors in the ERROR form that names the problem and the fix, not internals.

claude_md.paraphrase: Every MCP tool failure starts with ERROR: and names the problem and next action, without exception types or stack traces.

vision.paraphrase: The vision requires errors on non-MCP HTTP endpoints to follow the problem-details form with a useful next step.

claude_md.paraphrase: A failed request to a non-MCP HTTP endpoint returns an RFC 9457 problem-details body whose detail names the fix.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: The gateway refuses to start unless sign-in is configured, because an open gateway would spend the shared credit for anyone.

conops.paraphrase: The functional summary states the gateway refuses to start without sign-in configuration or the OpenRouter key, with no anonymous mode.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: Startup must fail when the organization's sign-in provider is not fully configured, so the gateway never runs without sign-in.

conops.paraphrase: The functional summary requires a refusal to start when sign-in configuration is missing, with no anonymous mode.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary / Gateway: sign-in and access
vision.paraphrase: The vision says the gateway refuses to start when the OpenRouter key is missing, so no caller can reach a gateway that cannot synthesize.

conops.paraphrase: The functional summary requires refusing to start without the OpenRouter key.

vision.paraphrase: The vision keeps tokens and keys out of logs, so the shared key and the sign-in secret must never be written there.

conops.paraphrase: The operational constraints say the OpenRouter key and the OIDC client secret come only from environment variables, which this test guards in the log.

vision.paraphrase: The SQLite database and cached audio files on the mounted volume hold the usage, quota and cache state that must survive a restart.

conops.paraphrase: The deployment constraint places the single container's data volume at a fixed path, which is where persisted state must live.
